fullPassage:
Astronaut Yujin's Space Log

Day 1 Back to Space!
After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!

Day 5 The World with No Gravity
Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.

Day 25 Starting the Day
The station orbits Earth once every 90 minutes, and the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes. However, our schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time on Earth.

My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything floats. Then, I look over the daily schedule sent by the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.

Every minute of an astronaut's day is planned by the Earth team. My work comprises lots of scientific experiments and maintenance of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day. Having green plants in space is a delight!

Day 60 Spacewalk!
Today's mission required a spacewalk, one of the riskiest tasks on the ISS. We had to install the bases for some newly developed solar batteries on the outside of the station.

Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed endless. Despite the safety cable, panic rose in me. I thought, "If my hand misses the handrail, I will fall into the void." The task seemed to take forever, but I finally managed to install the battery bases. When I turned my head, the bright blue Earth was still there. In the middle of darkness, its beauty was beyond description.

Day 99 One Day Left
I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is alarming and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, whose leaves have become a dense forest! All the same, I'll never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.

Day 100 The Descent to Earth
Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.

After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black. We were falling faster than the speed of sound. Once we got into the atmosphere about eight kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky until we hit the ground.

It's hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs. Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I'm home. I can smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I'll remember how magical these things are for the rest of my life.

questions.passage: After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest (A)[artificial / natural] space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth! Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often (B)[confused / certain] about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a (C)[random / precise] guess as to my position.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 가장 큰 인공(artificial) 우주 거주지, 몸 위치에 혼란스러운(confused), 무작위(random) 추측.
det.analysis:
✅ ① artificial — confused — random: 원문 일치
❌ ② natural: artificial의 반의어
❌ ③ certain: confused의 반의어
❌ ④ precise: random의 반의어
det.tip: artificial(인공) ↔ natural(자연). confused(혼란) ↔ certain(확실). random(무작위) ↔ precise(정확).

questions.passage: Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed (A)[endless / limited]. Despite the safety cable, (B)[panic / relief] rose in me. The task seemed to take forever, but I finally (C)[managed / failed] to install the battery bases.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ endless — panic — managed: 원문 일치
❌ ① limited: endless의 반의어
❌ ② relief: panic의 반의어
❌ ④ failed: managed의 반의어
det.tip: endless(끝없는) ↔ limited(제한된). panic(공포) ↔ relief(안도). managed(성공) ↔ failed(실패).

questions.passage: Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is (A)[resistant / welcoming] to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our (B)[descent / ascent]. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window. Once we got into the atmosphere about eight kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us with a (C)[sudden / gradual] halt.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② resistant — descent — sudden: 원문 일치
❌ ① welcoming: resistant의 반의어. 'didn't welcome with open arms' 단서
❌ ③ ascent: descent의 반의어. 지구로 내려오는 중
❌ ④ gradual: sudden의 반의어. 낙하산에 의한 급정지
det.tip: resistant(저항하는) ↔ welcoming. descent(하강) ↔ ascent(상승). sudden(갑작스러운) ↔ gradual(점진적).

questions.passage: I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is alarming and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically ①<u>harsh</u> things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the ②<u>satisfaction</u> of successfully finishing an experiment or a ③<u>challenging</u> task like a spacewalk. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ sparse(드문) → dense(빽빽한): 바질 잎이 '울창한' 숲이 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① harsh(가혹한): 원문 일치
✅ ② satisfaction(만족감): 원문 일치
✅ ③ challenging(도전적인): 원문 일치
❌ ④ sparse(드문) → dense(빽빽한) ← 정답
det.tip: dense(빽빽한) ↔ sparse(드문). 바질이 잘 자라서 울창해졌다는 문맥.

questions.passage:

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'everything floats'인데 'nothing floats'로 바뀜. 우주에서는 모든 것이 떠다니기 때문에 뱉을 수 없다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① lose(잃다): 원문 일치
✅ ② exercise(운동하다): 원문 일치
✅ ③ swallow(삼키다): 원문 일치
❌ ④ 원문 'everything' → 'nothing'으로 변경. spit 아닌 바로 뒤의 nothing이 오류 ← 정답
det.tip: everything floats(모든 것이 떠다님) ≠ nothing floats(아무것도 안 떠다님). 무중력 문맥.

questions.passage:

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ gently(부드럽게) → wildly(격렬하게): 낙하산이 캡슐을 격렬하게 흔들었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① heavier(더 무거운): 원문 일치
✅ ② scorched(그을린): 원문 일치
❌ ③ gently(부드럽게) → wildly(격렬하게): 하늘에서 격하게 흔들렸다 ← 정답
✅ ④ home(집): 원문 일치
det.tip: wildly(격렬하게) ↔ gently(부드럽게). 'dragged and swung wildly'가 원문.

questions.passage: Today's mission required a spacewalk, one of the <u>riskiest</u> tasks on the ISS. questions.stem: 밑줄 친 riskiest와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ most dangerous: riskiest와 동의어
❌ ① safest: 반의어
❌ ② easiest: 문맥 반대
❌ ④ most boring: 문맥 무관
det.tip: risky = dangerous = hazardous (위험한).

questions.passage: Every minute of an astronaut's day is planned by the Earth team. My work ____ lots of scientific experiments and maintenance of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day. Having green plants in space is a delight!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나의 업무는 많은 과학 실험과 정비를 포함한다(comprises).
det.analysis:
✅ ② comprises(포함하다): 원문 일치. 업무 내용 나열
❌ ① avoids(피하다): 업무를 피하는 것 아님
❌ ③ ignores(무시하다): 문맥 모순
❌ ④ destroys(파괴하다): 문맥 무관
det.tip: comprise = consist of = include (포함하다).

questions.passage: Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is ____ to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ resistant(저항하는): burn up from friction. 원문 일치
❌ ① welcoming(환영하는): 'didn't welcome with open arms' 단서
❌ ② friendly(친화적인): 물체를 태워버리므로 반대
❌ ③ helpful(도움이 되는): 진입 물체에 도움이 아님
det.tip: resistant to = ~에 저항하는. 대기가 물체 진입을 막는다.

det.analysis:

❌ ② brightness(밝음): 어둠과 반대
❌ ③ comfort(편안함): 공포 상황과 반대
❌ ④ crowd(군중): 우주 공간에 군중 없음
det.tip: void = emptiness = nothingness (공허, 빈 공간).

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 magical과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ wonderful(놀라운): magical과 동의어
❌ ① ordinary(평범한): magical의 반의어
❌ ② boring(지루한): magical의 반의어
❌ ④ terrible(끔찍한): magical의 반의어
det.tip: magical = wonderful = marvelous (경이로운).

questions.passage: I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is <u>alarming</u> and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 alarming과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② frightening(무서운): alarming과 동의어
❌ ① exciting(흥미진진한): 긍정적 뉘앙스
❌ ③ relaxing(편안한): alarming의 반의어
❌ ④ amusing(재미있는): 문맥 무관
det.tip: alarming = frightening = worrying (놀랍고 두려운).

questions.passage: After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked <u>successfully</u>. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 successfully와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ④ in vain(헛되이): successfully의 반의어. 성공적 도킹 ↔ 헛되이
❌ ① effectively(효과적으로): 동의어
❌ ② triumphantly(의기양양하게): 동의어
❌ ③ competently(능숙하게): 유의어
det.tip: successfully(성공적으로) ↔ in vain(헛되이). effectively, triumphantly는 비슷한 뜻.

questions.passage: In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. <u>Unfortunately</u>, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 Unfortunately와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① Fortunately(다행히): Unfortunately의 반의어
❌ ② Regrettably(유감스럽게): Unfortunately의 동의어
❌ ③ Sadly(슬프게도): Unfortunately의 동의어
❌ ④ Unluckily(불운하게): Unfortunately의 동의어
det.tip: Unfortunately(불행히) ↔ Fortunately(다행히). Regrettably, Sadly는 비슷한 뜻.

questions.passage:
(A) I click through new emails and <u>brush</u> my teeth.

(B) We moved along the handrail to the <u>edge</u> of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed endless.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 두 단어 brush와 edge의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ (A) 닦다 — (B) 가장자리: brush teeth = 이를 닦다, edge of the station = 정거장 끝
❌ ① (A) 붓: 명사가 아닌 동사 용법
❌ ② (B) 날카로움: 물리적 가장자리
❌ ④ 둘 다 틀림
det.tip: brush: ① 붓(명사) ② 닦다(동사). edge: ① 가장자리 ② 날카로움.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어를 고르시오.

"the force that causes things to fall towards the Earth and keeps planets in orbit around the sun"

det.korean: "물체를 지구로 떨어뜨리고 행성을 궤도에 유지하는 힘" → 중력(gravity)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ gravity(중력): 정의와 일치
❌ ① friction(마찰): 다른 물리적 힘
❌ ② pressure(압력): 다른 개념
❌ ③ density(밀도): 물질의 성질
det.tip: gravity(중력): 이 글의 핵심 개념. zero gravity = 무중력.

questions.passage: I'll miss the __________ (satisfy) of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: ✅ satisfaction: satisfy(동사) → satisfaction(명사). the _____ of 구조에서 명사 필요.
det.tip: satisfy → satisfaction: -faction 접미사. the + 명사 + of 구조.

questions.passage: Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the __________ (orbit) debris that would otherwise rain down on it.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: ✅ orbital: orbit(명사) → orbital(형용사). _____ debris 구조에서 형용사 필요.
det.tip: orbit → orbital: -al 접미사. 명사 앞 수식어이므로 형용사.

det.analysis:

❌ ② imagination(상상): 가능하지만 원문은 description
❌ ③ recognition(인식): 문맥과 덜 어울림
❌ ④ expectation(기대): 문맥과 무관
det.tip: beyond description = 말로 표현할 수 없는. 관용 표현.

det.analysis:
✅ ② readjusting(재적응하는): 무중력 환경에 뇌가 다시 적응. 원문 일치
❌ ① surrendering(항복하는): 적응이지 항복 아님
